_about: WORDS THREE, HIS HOMEWORK, SHEET SIX: OUR TRY ON EVERY CARD (VAMILY rules 467 amended 11/22, 470(g), 465; ask rows 629, 666). He answered every card of sheets one to five, so the tab was empty. Rule 467 amended: every card shows OUR TRY in the voice beside the line the game says now, so he sees what we learned; at least two tries in three on a sheet carry a real curse in full; the ones who would not curse are left clean on purpose, each card saying why ('clean'). Every try follows THE VOICE so far: never 'it pays' (470(g): a person says who pays and what, or nothing), no battery count in a feeling, say it like a person, no fashion names as a joke, plain beats clever. Here: 10 of 12 tries curse; the sergeant and the church radio are clean on purpose. Our tries are on the cards only: nothing in the game is rewritten until he says he is done (rule 465). tools/bohemia_words_two_homework.js reads every game line out of its file; the tries are ours and marked so.
said: you show me one sentence or one dialog caption that you made and then I'll tell you how I want that shit to sound

cards.rule: NEVER 'IT PAYS': a job giver says who pays and what
cards.mouth: A JOB GIVER AT THE BOARD
cards.who_plain: The man who keeps the dam's turbines
cards.when: you ask what his job is and what you get for it
cards.where: in a camp or TOWN, at the board where people offer jobs
cards.try: Two of my pump posts on the dam road went quiet this week. Quiet out there means some motherfucker is sitting on them, listening. Walk out to both and come back breathing, and I'll pay you {pay} batteries out of the turbine money myself.
cards.teaches: YOUR 'IT PAYS' NO, FIXED ON THE BIGGEST MOUTH: 20 of the 102 job lines say 'it pays'; ours says who pays (him, out of the turbine money) and what

cards.rule: THEY CURSE, AND WHO DOES NOT: a sergeant asking strangers for help
cards.role: stops your crew on the road with his patrol
cards.who_plain: A sergeant of the Blues with a patrol one gun short
cards.when: raiders just hit a farm and he needs one more gun
cards.where: on the MAP, on the card that stops your crew on the road
cards.try: Raiders hit a farm west of here. The family's still in the house. We're one gun short. Ride with us one hour and I'll pay you out of my own pocket, and the Blues don't forget who stood with us.
cards.clean: a sergeant asking strangers for help, with his own men listening, keeps it clean
cards.teaches: WHERE THE CURSING STOPS: a disciplined man asking for help; we left him clean on purpose; and who pays is him

cards.rule: THEY CURSE: grief and a threat in one breath
cards.who_plain: A man whose radio you took the batteries out of
cards.when: he catches up with you on the road
cards.where: on the MAP, on the card that stops your crew on the road
cards.try: You took the batteries out of my fucking radio. My wife recorded that report the morning before she died. That's the last of her voice I've got. Put four back, or I swear to God I follow you till one of us is dead.
cards.teaches: THEY CURSE AT THE WORST MOMENT: a widower threatening armed men over his dead wife's voice

cards.rule: THEY CURSE: men who ran from what they did
cards.role: men who walked away from their crew
cards.who_plain: Two men who deserted the Reds
cards.when: they step out of the brush and ask to join you
cards.where: on the MAP, on the card that stops your crew on the road
cards.try: We quit the Reds. They had us shooting water thieves, kids, fucking everybody. We can fight. Take us or don't, but if the Reds hear you saw us, we're dead men.
cards.teaches: THEY CURSE ABOUT WHAT THEY DID: shame and fear from armed men; 'everybody' carries the curse

cards.rule: THEY CURSE: the enemy's why (your raiders NO: 'They not cursing bro')
cards.role: leads the men who keep the animals
cards.who_plain: The leader of the men who keep a herd of lab animals
cards.when: a fight opens on the road and his animals come at you
cards.where: on the card that opens a FIGHT
cards.try: The herd's starving, and you dumb fucks walked right up to their dinner.
cards.teaches: THE WHY LINE CURSES: 163 why lines, none curse; your raiders card said so; this is our try on the next one

cards.rule: THEY CURSE: a miss in the middle of a fight
cards.when: one of your men misses a shot he should have made
cards.where: in a FIGHT, over his head
cards.try: Hit the fucking man, not the air!
cards.teaches: THEY CURSE, THE SMALLEST LINE: 584 lines over his men's heads; one word added is the whole change

cards.rule: THEY CURSE: a man who prays, after he has won
cards.who_plain: The man in your crew who prays
cards.where: on the screen after a FIGHT
cards.try: We pray for them later. Grab their shit first.
cards.teaches: THE PRAYING MAN, AFTER: outnumbered he was clean ('Lord, that is a lot of them', your YES); after a win he loots; does a believer curse here

cards.rule: THEY CURSE: an Elder three nights after a raid
cards.mouth: THE ELDER OF A RAIDED TOWN
cards.role: of a town raided three nights ago
cards.who_plain: The head of a town that was just raided
cards.when: you walk into a town a crew burned three nights ago
cards.where: in a TOWN, when you open it
cards.try: A crew came through three nights ago. They burned the Ortegas' house with the grandmother still inside. Half of what we had walked out the gate with those sons of bitches.
cards.teaches: YOUR STARRED ELDER WAS PEACEFUL AND CLEAN; this one is grieving and angry; does an Elder curse when it is his town that burned

cards.rule: THEY CURSE: a man selling himself as dangerous
cards.who_plain: A man the casinos used to send to collect debts
cards.when: you look at him in the hire line
cards.where: in a TOWN, on the card of a man for hire
cards.try: I did collections for the casinos. Nobody paid me late twice, and the ones who tried still can't fucking walk right.
cards.teaches: A HIRE SELLS HIMSELF BY HOW DANGEROUS HE IS (your 'real deal killers'); our try adds what happened to the ones who were late

cards.rule: THEY CURSE: the one who sends you after a boss
cards.when: she stops you to send you after the boss who makes the guns
cards.where: on the MAP, on the card that starts a boss's trail
cards.try: You want guns? Everybody wants guns. The Machinist makes them and sells them to whoever has batteries, and he throws nails on every street around his shop so you crawl in on your fucking knees. Ask at the bar, every drunk in there knows him.
cards.teaches: THE ASKER, THE FURTHEST MOUTH: your trucker card was a YES as it stood; this asker is angry and curses; which is right for the 60 asker lines

cards.rule: THEY CURSE, AND WHO DOES NOT: a church under attack, on the radio
cards.who_plain: The guard at a church town's gate, on the radio
cards.when: armed men are at the fence and say nobody is coming
cards.where: on the phone's FEED, while the town falls
cards.try: He says nobody's coming. He said it nice, like he was sorry. God help us.
cards.clean: a church's radio while the children hide in the crypt; your own radio call did not curse ('God help us...')
cards.teaches: WHERE THE CURSING STOPS: your radio call was clean, a prayer at the end; our try keeps this one clean on purpose and in capitals like yours

cards.rule: NEVER 'IT PAYS', AND THEY CURSE: a gambler says who pays what
cards.who_plain: An old casino dealer on the road with a deck of cards
cards.when: he offers you one hand of high card
cards.where: on the MAP, on the card that stops your crew on the road
cards.try: One hand, high card. You win, I give you twenty batteries. You lose, I take ten. The house always won, and look at this shit now, the house is dead. Deal?
cards.teaches: WHO PAYS, SAID RIGHT: the dealer says exactly who gives what to whom ('I give you twenty'); our try drops 'mijo' and adds the curse
